title: optimize cpu request path: reduce serialization, pin thread pools, and improve batching
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: production incidents and lab profiling showed CPU-side bottlenecks on the serving request path: excessive serialization allocations, lock contention in KV cache reads, and suboptimal scheduling of continuous batching which amplified tail latency. This PR implements a set of coordinated changes to reduce CPU overhead and stabilize tail latency. Key changes: 1) Move heavy serialization off the hot request path into a configurable serialization worker pool and introduce a compact binary fast-path for common small requests, with pre-allocated buffers to avoid repeated heap allocations. 2) Introduce configurable thread pinning for worker and batcher threads (sched_setaffinity on Linux) and expose per-role affinity groups in the instance config; default pins prefer isolated high-performance cores. 3) Rework request thread pool to use an MPSC enqueue with per-shard queues to reduce global contention and add a lightweight backpressure signal for the batcher to avoid busy-wait loops. 4) Reduce KV cache contention by sharding the cache and adding a read-optimized fast path that avoids writer locks for hit-heavy workloads; also added metrics for shard hit/miss and lock waiting time. 5) Batch scheduler heuristics: improved coalescing for short-lived bursts, reduced wakeup frequency, and a soft-deadline path to flush long-waiting small batches. Tests and validation: unit tests for new serialization worker and affinity config, fuzzing for the binary fast-path, and an end-to-end load harness used for benchmarks. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves prior semantics unless affinity or fast-path flags are enabled in config. Rollout plan: staged canary on Dedicated clusters with 5% traffic for 6h then 25% for 24h; automatic rollback if 95th latency regresses >10%. Motivation and tradeoffs: moving serialization out of the critical path adds bounded scheduling latency but dramatically reduces GC/alloc stalls in the hot path; thread pinning improves cache locality at the cost of less flexible CPU packing, so pins are configurable per deployment. Benchmarks: on our benchmark-lab on an 8-vGPU Dedicated node serving short prompts, 95th percentile latency dropped from 140ms to 65ms, p50 from 32ms to 22ms, overall throughput increased ~28% at target SLO, CPU system-time dropped ~18%, and KV cache read lock waits reduced by >70%. Also included are CI and canary playbook snippets in docs.

review_comments: Evan Liu: Can you quantify the scheduling delay added by moving serialization into a worker pool? Suggest a default budget attr for the worker so we don't regress p50.
Priya Nair: Measured median scheduling overhead at ~0.4ms in our harness; added a configurable per-pool max-latency and a fast-path that bypasses the worker for very small frames.
Marco Alvarez: Thread pinning LGTM but please add opt-out and document behavior on oversubscription; also add unit tests that simulate low core counts.
Priya Nair: Added opt-out flag and tests for 2-core and 4-core simulated nodes; documented in instance-affinity.md.
Sara Blake: KV shard read fast-path looks correct but add metrics for write skew and rebalancing; consider exponential backoff when acquiring writer lock.
Priya Nair: Added lock_waits.metric and kv-cache contention alert with exponential backoff suggestion for writer lock acquisition.
